Aṅguttara-Nikāya. XI.

Just as, venerable sir, a dust-cloth wipes clean things and wipes dirty things, wipes away excrement and wipes away urine, wipes away spittle and wipes away pus, and wipes away blood, yet the dust-cloth is not thereby troubled or disgusted: even so, venerable sir, I dwell with a mind like a dust-cloth, extensive, exalted, measureless, without enmity, and without ill-will. Whoever, venerable sir, has not established mindfulness of the body regarding his own body, he might offend a fellow practitioner here and depart on his travels without seeking forgiveness.

Just as, venerable sir, a low-caste boy or a low-caste girl, carrying a basket <note>original: "kaḷopihattho"</note> and wearing rags, enters a village or town having adopted a humble attitude: even so, venerable sir, I dwell with a mind like a low-caste boy, extensive, exalted, measureless, without enmity, and without ill-will. Whoever, venerable sir, has not established mindfulness of the body regarding his own body, he might offend a fellow practitioner here and depart on his travels without seeking forgiveness.

Just as, venerable sir, a bull with broken horns, gentle, well-tamed, and well-trained, wandering from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads, does not harm anyone with its foot or its horns: even so, venerable sir, I dwell with a mind like a bull with broken horns, extensive, exalted, measureless, without enmity, and without ill-will. Whoever, venerable sir, has not established mindfulness of the body regarding his own body, he might offend a fellow practitioner here and depart on his travels without seeking forgiveness.

Just as, venerable sir, a woman or a man, whether young or in the prime of life, fond of decoration, having washed their head, with a corpse of a snake <note>original: "ahikuṇapena"</note> or...

<summary>The Buddha describes three similes—the dust-cloth, the low-caste youth, and the hornless bull—to illustrate the cultivation of a mind that is patient, humble, and non-violent toward others.</summary>
